item.title: How Much Is Too Much? Sizing a Small Bet
item.description: How much of my savings should be in bitcoin? Any amount whose loss would touch your real life is too much. Size it like hot sauce: a small dash on a full meal.

item.title: What an HSA Actually Is (and Who It's For)
item.description: What is an HSA in simple terms? A health savings account: money in untaxed, money out for health untaxed, and it's yours to keep. Plus the catch about who can open one.

item.title: What a Bitcoin Wallet Actually Is
item.description: What is a bitcoin wallet, in simple terms? It's a mailbox: an address anyone can send to, and a key only you should open. The coins live on a shared record.

item.title: The Real Cost of Carrying a Credit Card Balance
item.description: Why does my credit card balance never go down? The interest is a hole in the boat and the minimum payment barely bails it. Here's how to actually drain it.

item.title: "Not Your Keys" — What That Warning Actually Means
item.description: What does "not your keys, not your coins" mean? If someone else holds your bitcoin, you have a promise, not the cash. Self-custody explained plainly, upsides and downsides.

item.title: Who Gets the New Money First (and Why It's Not You)
item.description: Why do the rich get richer with inflation? New money reaches them first, before prices rise. Regular people are last in line. Explained with a buffet line.

item.title: Who Health Sharing Is Wrong For
item.description: Is health sharing a bad idea? For some people, yes. It's wrong for you if you have ongoing medical needs, need a legal guarantee, or the rules don't fit your life.

item.title: Bitcoin's Wild Price Swings, Explained Calmly
item.description: Why is bitcoin so volatile, and is it normal? It's a young, small road that isn't paved yet, so every bump feels big. Explained calmly, with what the swings do and don't mean.

item.title: Why Prices Climb but the News Says Inflation's Down
item.description: Why are prices still high if inflation went down? Because inflation is the speed prices rise, not the prices. The hill got less steep; you're still climbing.

item.title: Health Sharing vs. Insurance: The Honest Trade-offs
item.description: Health sharing vs. insurance, pros and cons laid side by side. Cost, the legal guarantee, what's covered, and the incentive, explained plainly with a potluck.

item.title: Why I Don't Try to Time the Price
item.description: Should you wait for bitcoin to drop before you buy? Almost nobody times the market. Here's why I don't try, and the calm habit I use instead.

item.title: Stop Renting Your Subscriptions a Mansion
item.description: How to cut subscriptions you forgot about: a 20-minute statement walk-through. Turn off the lights in the empty rooms and move that money to savings.

item.title: Health Insurance's Built-In Conflict of Interest
item.description: Do insurance companies want to deny claims? They earn more when they pay out less. It's a built-in conflict of interest, explained with a referee paid by one team.

item.title: A Little Each Week Beats Betting It All
item.description: What is dollar-cost averaging? Buying a little on a set schedule instead of betting it all at once. Be the steady faucet, not the one big bucket.

item.title: A Budget That Survives a Busy Week
item.description: A simple budget for people with no time. Three lines, one spending number to watch, and a save-first move on payday. Built for a real, busy week.

item.title: Why Hard-to-Make Money Holds Its Value
item.description: What makes money hold its value over time? Difficulty. Hard-to-make money holds value; easy-to-make money gets watered down. Explained with two IOUs and gold.

item.title: What a Deductible Really Means (No Jargon)
item.description: What is a deductible in simple terms? It's the part of a medical bill you pay before insurance pays anything. Plus premium, copay, and out-of-pocket max, explained plainly.

item.title: The Dollar's Slow Leak, Explained Simple
item.description: Why does money lose value over time? Because more dollars can always be made. Here's inflation explained simply, with a slow-leaking tire.

item.title: Your First $20 in Bitcoin, Step by Step
item.description: Want to try bitcoin without risking much? Here's how to buy your first $20, step by step, using money you can afford to lose. Plain English, no hype.

item.title: The $500 Question: How One Health Event Gets Paid
item.description: How does health sharing actually pay a big medical bill? You cover the first $500, the bill gets negotiated down, and the crowd covers the rest. Here's how.
